We evaluate the models here against a large number of simulated chronologies and
radiocarbon samples. To save ourselves some time, we also run these simulations
in parallel. Generally speaking, running torch models in parallel is a bad idea
since torch has built-in parallelism that could lead to thread contests. We try
to account for this by limiting the number of threads in each parallel process
to one. Running my PC at full tilt on 14 of 16 cores reduces the total wall time
(in hours) for the evaluation by an order of magnitude.

Each simulation looks like the example above, following the generative model.
The steps are as follows:

1. Sample a starting year.
2. Simulate a chronology.
3. Sample dates from the chronology.
4. Calibrate the dates.
5. Train models with dates.
6. Infer chronology and sample ages.
7. Evaluate models.

These steps are repeated for each simulation. Currently, there are 3 (n_years)
$\times$ 3 (n_samples) $\times$ 3 (n_clusters) $\times$ 3 (distribution) = 81 
starting conditions that are repeated 28 times each, resulting in 2268 unique 
simulations with randomization.

**Metrics**

Calibration metrics compare age estimates $\hat{t}_{i}$, drawn from each
sample's posterior given its calibrated date $F_{i}$, against true ages
$t_{i}$ for $n$ samples. $\hat{t}_{i}'$ is an independent draw from the same
posterior.

$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{MAE} &= \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^{n} \hspace{2pt} \mathbb{E} \left| [\hat{t}_{i} \mid F_{i}] - t_{i} \right| \\
\text{MSE} &= \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^{n} \hspace{2pt} \mathbb{E} \left( [\hat{t}_{i} \mid F_{i}] - t_{i} \right)^{2} \\
\text{CRPS} &= \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^{n} \hspace{2pt} \mathbb{E} \left| \hat{t}_{i} - t_{i} \right| - \frac{1}{2} \mathbb{E} \left| \hat{t}_{i} - \hat{t}_{i}' \right| \\
\text{LP} &= -\frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^{n} \hspace{2pt} \log p(t_{i} \mid F_{i}, \hat{v})
\end{aligned}
$$

Summary metrics compare the estimated density $\hat{v}$ against the true
density $v$ over $m$ years, where $V_{j}$ and $\hat{V}_{j}$ are their
cumulative sums.

$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{TVD} &= 0.5 \sum_{j=1}^{m} \hspace{2pt} \left| v_{j} - \hat{v}_{j} \right| \\
\text{WD} &= \sum_{j=1}^{m} \hspace{2pt} \left| V_{j} - \hat{V}_{j} \right|
\end{aligned}
$$

Only CRPS (as recovery against the oracle) and TVD are reported in the paper.
The other metrics are reported here as supplementary checks.

**Simulations**

```{r}
#| label: evaluation-scenarios
n_clusters <- 14

evaluation_grid <- expand.grid(
  n_years = c(500, 2500, 12500),
  n_samples = c(50, 250, 1250),
  n_clusters = c(1, 3, 9),
  distribution = c("gaussian", "uniform", "skewed"),
  replicate = seq_len(n_clusters * 2),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

n_iter <- nrow(evaluation_grid)
```

Each worker process runs one simulation at a time, picking up the next as soon
as it finishes. Every simulation gets a unique index, which sets its random
seed, so results do not depend on which worker runs it or when.

```{r}
#| label: model-evaluation
#| cache: true
#| time_it: true
#| output: false

# set up clusters
clusters <- makeCluster(n_clusters)

fns <- c(
  "bgmm.R",
  "calibrate.R",
  "ckde.R",
  "constants.R",
  "dataframe-helpers.R",
  "dpmm.R",
  "metrics.R",
  "mixture-helpers.R",
  "netc14.R",
  "sample-dates.R",
  "simulate-chronology.R",
  "spd.R"
)

clusterExport(
  clusters,
  varlist = c("fns", "intcal20", "evaluation_grid"),
  envir = environment()
)

clusterEvalQ(clusters, {
  library(carbondate)
  library(torch)
  torch_set_num_threads(1)
  lapply(file.path("R", fns), source)
})

# run simulations in parallel, one scenario at a time
evaluation_results <- parLapplyLB(clusters, seq_len(n_iter), \(iter) {
  set.seed(STARTREK + iter)

  # scenario
  n_years <- evaluation_grid[["n_years"]][iter]
  n_clusters <- evaluation_grid[["n_clusters"]][iter]
  n_samples <- evaluation_grid[["n_samples"]][iter]
  distribution <- evaluation_grid[["distribution"]][iter]
  start <- sample(seq(100, 49500 - n_years), 1)
  end <- start + n_years - 1

  # simulate chronology, draw samples, and calibrate
  chronology <- simulate_chronology(start, end, n_clusters, distribution)
  samples <- sample_dates(chronology, n_samples, intcal20)
  calibrated_dates <- calibrate(samples, intcal20)

  # training
  models <- list(
    ckde(calibrated_dates),
    bgmm(calibrated_dates),
    dpmm(samples),
    netc(calibrated_dates),
    spd(calibrated_dates)
  )

  # evaluation
  years <- seq(start, end)
  true_ages <- samples[["cal_age"]]
  true_years <- true_ages - start + 1

  # plug-in posterior of each sample's age given a global density
  posterior <- function(v) {
    q <- t(t(calibrated_dates) * v)
    q / rowSums(q)
  }

  evaluations <- lapply(models, \(.model) {
    .density <- density(.model, years)[["density"]]
    .ages <- predict(.model, calibrated_dates)

    data.frame(
      tvd = tvd(.density, chronology),
      wd = wd(.density, chronology),
      mae = mae(.ages, true_ages),
      mse = mse(.ages, true_ages),
      crps = crps(.ages, true_ages),
      lp = lp(posterior(.density), true_years)
    )
  })

  evaluations <- do.call(rbind, evaluations)

  # baseline
  oracle_ages <- predict(chronology, calibrated_dates)
  mae_oracle <- mae(oracle_ages, true_ages)
  mse_oracle <- mse(oracle_ages, true_ages)
  crps_oracle <- crps(oracle_ages, true_ages)
  lp_oracle <- lp(posterior(unclass(chronology)), true_years)

  # collect and return
  e_clusters <- vapply(models, count_components, integer(1))
  elapsed <- sapply(models, attr, which = "elapsed")

  sim <- data.frame(
    iter = iter,
    model = c("CKDE", "BGMM", "DPMM", "NetC14", "SPD"),
    start = start,
    n_years = n_years,
    n_samples = n_samples,
    n_clusters = n_clusters,
    distribution = distribution,
    e_clusters = e_clusters,
    mae_oracle = mae_oracle,
    mse_oracle = mse_oracle,
    crps_oracle = crps_oracle,
    lp_oracle = lp_oracle,
    elapsed = elapsed
  )

  cbind(sim, evaluations)
})

# close parallel processes and collect results
stopCluster(clusters)
evaluation_results <- do.call(rbind, evaluation_results)
```

Save results.

```{r}
#| label: save-evaluation
write.csv(
  evaluation_results,
  "data/evaluation-results.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)
```
